claims.text: The initial nanoparticle state is a single-phase solid solution.
Thermal energy available during synthesis governs formation of noble-metal-based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
Kinetic pathways available during synthesis govern formation of noble-metal-based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
The balance of thermal energy and kinetic pathways governs crystal-structure selection and phase stability.
Varying synthesis temperature at constant composition will produce tunable crystal structure and phase stability.
Varying heating and cooling rates at constant composition will produce tunable crystal structure and phase stability.
Thermal decomposition and elemental segregation mediate the structural response to synthesis conditions.
Changing synthesis temperature and heating/cooling rates may change particle morphology.
Changing synthesis temperature and heating/cooling rates may change elemental segregation.
Changing synthesis temperature and heating/cooling rates may induce or alter phase separation.
The proposed processing range is 500–1000 °C with heating and cooling rates of 1–10 °C/min.
An absence of significant crystal-structure and phase-stability changes across the varied synthesis conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
